'''Theresa M. Reineke''' (born January 1, 1972) is an American chemist and Distinguished McKnight University Professor at the [[University of Minnesota]]. She designs sustainable, environmentally friendly polymer-based delivery systems for targeted therapeutics. She is the associate editor of ''[[ACS Macro Letters]]''.

== Early life and education ==
Reineke earned her bachelor's degree at [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Eau Claire]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://reinekegroup.org/group/dr-theresa-m-reineke|title=Dr. Theresa M. Reineke|website=The Reineke Group|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-17|archive-date=2019-04-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412173337/http://reinekegroup.org/group/dr-theresa-m-reineke|url-status=dead}}</ref> She moved to [[Arizona State University]] for her graduate studies and earned a master's degree in 1998.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://breakthroughsymposium.com/schedule/theresa-m-reineke/|title=Nonviral Synthetic Polymers Promote Cellular and In Vivo Delivery of Therapeutic Genes and Editing Systems|website=Breakthrough Symposium|access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> Reineke was a PhD student at the [[University of Michigan]], where she was supervised by Michael O'Keeffe and [[Omar M. Yaghi]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=67659|title=Chemistry Tree – Theresa M. Reineke|website=academictree.org|access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> She was awarded the Wirt and Mary Cornell Prize for Outstanding Graduate Research. Reineke joined the [[California Institute of Technology]] as an [[National Institutes of Health]] postdoctoral fellow in 2000.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Reineke joined the [[University of Minnesota]] in 2011. Her research group focus on the design, characterisation and functionalisation of macromolecular systems.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://reinekegroup.org/research|title=Research|website=The Reineke Group|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-17|archive-date=2019-04-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425114045/http://reinekegroup.org/research|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Aldevron|title=Theresa Reineke; Breakthrough Symposium Presenter|date=2018-12-04|url=https://vimeo.com/304455913|access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> These macromolecules include biocompatible polymers that can deliver [[DNA]] for regenerative medicine as well as targeted therapeutic treatments.<ref name=":1" /> She was made a Lloyd H. Reyerson Professor with tenure at the University of Minnesota in 2011.<ref name=":0" /> Reineke has published over 140 papers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Publications Archive - Page 2 of 2 - The Reineke Group |url=https://reinekegroup.org/publications/page/2 |access-date=2023-10-13 |language=en-US |archive-date=2024-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240305075124/https://reinekegroup.org/publications/page/2/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Nucleic acid]]s can have an unparalleled [[chemical specificity|specificity]] for targets inside a cell, but need to be compacted into nanostructures ([[polyplex]]es) that can enter cells.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://reinekegroup.org/nucleic-acid-delivery|title=Nucleic Acid Delivery|website=The Reineke Group|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-17|archive-date=2019-04-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190409183643/http://reinekegroup.org/nucleic-acid-delivery|url-status=live}}</ref> Reineke designs polymer-based transportation systems for nucleic acids.<ref name=":2" /> These polymer vehicles can improve the solubility and bioavailability of drugs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.stanford.edu/group/polymercollective/cgi-bin/wordpress/?p=3611|title=2019 Winter Talk (Theresa M. Reineke, University of Minnesota) {{!}} Stanford Polymer Collective|last1=Stanford|first1=© Stanford University|last2=Notice|first2=California 94305 Copyright Complaints Trademark|website=web.stanford.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-04-17|archive-date=2022-12-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226011124/https://web.stanford.edu/group/polymercollective/cgi-bin/wordpress/?p=3611|url-status=dead}}</ref> These often incorporate [[carbohydrate]]s, which have an affinity for polyplexes and are non-toxic.<ref name=":2" /> She is a member of the University of Minnesota Centre for Sustainable Polymers, synthesising polymers from sustainable ingredients. The carbohydrate units within her polymer drug delivery systems are a widely available, renewable resource.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=http://reinekegroup.org/sustainable-polymers|title=Sustainable Polymers|website=The Reineke Group|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-17|archive-date=2019-04-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190418113657/http://reinekegroup.org/sustainable-polymers|url-status=dead}}</ref> The sustainable polymers designed by Reineke include [[Polyester|poly(ester]]-[[thioether]]s).<ref name=":3" />

Reineke used [[reversible addition−fragmentation chain-transfer polymerization]] for the synthesis of diblock [[terpolymer]]s that can be used for targeted drug delivery.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://reinekegroup.org/oral-drug-delivery|title=Oral Drug Delivery|website=The Reineke Group|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> She used [[Spray drying|spray dried]] dispersions of the polymer with the drug [[probucol]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tale|first1=Swapnil|last2=Purchel|first2=Anatolii A.|last3=Dalsin|first3=Molly C.|last4=Reineke|first4=Theresa M.|date=2017-09-22|title=Diblock Terpolymers Are Tunable and pH Responsive Vehicles To Increase Hydrophobic Drug Solubility for Oral Administration|journal=Molecular Pharmaceutics|volume=14|issue=11|pages=4121–4127|doi=10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.7b00458|pmid=28937226|issn=1543-8384}}</ref>

Reineke was made a University of Minnesota Distinguished McKnight University Professor in 2017.<ref name=":0" /> She is the associate editor of ''[[ACS Macro Letters]]'' and on the Advisory Board of ''[[Biomacromolecules]]'', ''[[Bioconjugate Chemistry]]'' and ''[[Polymer Chemistry (journal)|Polymer Chemistry]]''.<ref name=":0"/> She is a member of the [[American Chemical Society]] Polymer Division.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://old.polyacs.org/211.html|title=Reineke – address|website=old.polyacs.org|access-date=2019-04-17|archive-date=2019-04-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417214955/http://old.polyacs.org/211.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Her work has been supported by an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]], a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]], the [[National Institutes of Health]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Database {{!}} Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |access-date=2022-03-24 |website=sloan.org |language=en |archive-date=2022-06-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220618214036/https://sloan.org/fellows-database |url-status=live }}</ref>
